column4: The active market is set entirely by a client writable cookie that is forwarded verbatim as the highest precedence input to the backend
column5: The market cookie is written by client JavaScript through setCookie which uses document.cookie so it cannot be httpOnly (src/lib/cookies.ts:12-51) and is set that way by resolveMarketForCountry at src/helpers/market.ts:19. On the server render path getMarketFromContext reads it straight from the request cookie header (src/helpers/functionalHelpers.ts:600-610) and passes it as params.market - and the request interceptor turns that into the X-Market header (src/routes/interceptor.ts:40-52). Nothing at any point validates that the value is a real market code or that the customer is entitled to it. CLAUDE.md section 7.4 records the panel DetectMarket precedence as X-Market header first then the ?market= query then the user_market pivot then the cookie - so the value the client controls outranks the account own market. PROVEN BY TEST: a dev server was run against a mock backend that logs headers - a single request for /brands/ carrying a hand written cookie of market=ZZ-ARBITRARY produced exactly two backend calls and BOTH carried X-Market: ZZ-ARBITRARY. ZZ-ARBITRARY is not a real market code and it was forwarded unchanged. WHAT IS NOT VERIFIABLE HERE - whether the panel rejects an unknown code and whether it checks entitlement before pricing in that market.

column12: 1. Set the market cookie to an arbitrary value in devtools. 2. Load any catalogue page. 3. Observe on the backend that X-Market carries the supplied value on every request from that page.
column13: The panel validates the market code and the caller entitlement to it - and pricing follows the market the account and the delivery address actually belong to rather than a client assertion.
column14: Any string the client puts in the cookie is forwarded as the top precedence market input.
column15: If the panel prices from the client asserted market without checking entitlement a customer can shop and check out at another market prices - which is direct financial loss through arbitrage. If it merely fails on an unknown code the practical impact is limited to a broken page. The storefront cannot tell which is the case and provides no bound either way.
column16: Confirm with the panel team that DetectMarket rejects unknown codes and validates entitlement before pricing - and that the order placement path re-derives the market from the delivery address rather than trusting the request header. On the storefront side treat the market as server owned: stop writing the cookie from client code and take the active market from the settings response after /markets/switch.
